summary: RR_PROJECT_BULATOVA_POPP is a Python package designed for automated statistical hypothesis testing and data visualization. The package dynamically selects parametric or non-parametric tests (T-Test, Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney U, ANOVA, Alexander-Govern, Kruskal-Wallis) based on data characteristics (normality, variance homogeneity) and provides integrated visual diagnostics.
strengths: Object-oriented structure using an abstract base class (StatisticalTest) to define a common interface.
Automated selection of statistical tests depending on distribution (normality) and variance properties.
Integrated visualization diagnostics (histograms with normal PDF overlays, Q-Q plots, joyplots, boxplots).
Thorough input checking inside class constructors (type verification, non-finite values, and size checks).
issues: Build and package metadata artifacts (build/ and RR_PROJECT_BULATOVA_POPP.egg-info/) are committed to the git repository.
Compatibility issue with modern SciPy versions where st.mode() returns ModeResult instead of a scalar value, breaking descriptive statistics representation.
Typographical spelling errors (e.g., 'not_lurge_length' in AnovaTestClass/IndependentTestClass and 'lenght' in PairedTestClass).
Hardcoded plt.show() calls within library classes block script/notebook execution and limit figure reuse.
ANOVA variance checking defaults to False, bypassing automated homoscedasticity checks.
Independent t-test lacks an automated check for variance homogeneity to automatically choose between Student's T and Welch's T.
recommendations: Add build/ and .egg-info/ directories to .gitignore and remove them from version control.
Update st.mode(arr) to handle modern SciPy ModeResult objects correctly (e.g., extracting .mode[0]).
Correct spelling typos ('not_lurge_length' to 'not_large_length' and 'lenght' to 'length').
Refactor visualization methods to return Matplotlib Figure/Axes objects instead of calling plt.show() directly.
Implement automated variance checking in IndependentTtest to decide if equal_var should be True or False.
Improve path portability by using os.path or pathlib in examples and documentation.
